Thanks for the loop, Irene. Quick answer and proposed playbook below.

Short answer: If Heliotron provides a valid UK VAT registration and VIES confirms the number, we should NOT charge UK VAT and instead treat the sale under reverse-charge (customer accounting). Practically we do a credit note for the original invoice and reissue a replacement invoice net of VAT. We also tag the transactions for local tax reporting and update the invoice metadata to reference the credit note.

Proposed steps (recommended):
1) Validate VAT number via VIES now (I can run this). If VIES passes, request the customer to upload the VAT certificate to our evidence portal (link below).
2) Finance issues a credit note for Invoice 2026-094 and issues Invoice 2026-094-RC (net of VAT). Mark both records with memo: "Reverse-charge applied per customer VAT confirmation" and add HubSpot deal note DL-4821.
3) Update accounting tags for the EU entity (use tax code RC-UK-2026). Jonas — can you confirm the correct ledger mapping?
4) Release payment hold once reissued invoice is in system; ask for payment within 10 business days of reissue.
5) Retain VAT certificate and VIES validation screenshot in the evidence folder.

Attachments: VAT validation checklist (vat-validation-checklist.pdf) — it lists accepted docs (scanned certificate + VIES status screenshot).

Alex — if you can upload the certificate to our portal it speeds the flow. If anything fails, we’ll advise next steps (likely we will collect VAT and follow our normal VAT filing).

—Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
